notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces WebChoreArena, 532 web chores built on WebArena environments to evaluate agents’ retention of page information, calculation, and tracking across pages.

name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.

name: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Mirage-1 organizes interaction trajectories into execution, core, and meta-skills, then uses them to guide Monte Carlo tree search during online GUI tasks. It introduces AndroidLH for long-horizon evaluation and tests the approach on Android and web-navigation benchmarks.

name: Context manipulation attacks : Web agents are susceptible to corrupted memory
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies context manipulation in web agents by altering stored task representations rather than webpage prompts alone. Evaluation on Browser-use and Agent-E examines memory-directed attacks and the implications for secure context handling.

name: Chain-of-Memory: Enhancing GUI Agents for Cross-Application Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Memory explicitly records action descriptions and task-relevant screen information in short- and long-term memory for GUI navigation. GUI Odyssey-CoM provides 111,000 screen-action pairs with memory annotations for learning and evaluating information retention across applications.

name: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebArxiv provides 510 static-snapshot tasks with deterministic answers for scholarly browsing, including constrained paper retrieval, content extraction, and cross-paper comparison. The study also tests dynamic retrieval of interaction history to address repetitive or incomplete agent reasoning.

name: MapAgent: Trajectory-Constructed Memory-Augmented Planning for Mobile Task Automation
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds reusable page memories from past mobile trajectories and retrieves them to support task planning and execution.

name: WebSight: A Vision-First Architecture for Robust Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebSight uses a vision-language model trained on web-interface examples within a modular agent with planning, action, verification, and episodic memory components. It evaluates element clicking on Showdown Clicks and full browsing tasks on WebVoyager using visual observations.

name: PerPilot: Personalizing VLM-based Mobile Agents via Memory and Exploration
notes: Personalization depends on the validity of stored or inferred user information and retrieval access. This is instruction completion with interaction, not demonstrated permanent model-weight personalization. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (The Framework of PerPilot; Personalization Perception; Personalization Completion; PerInstruct Data Construction).
summary: Introduces PerPilot and the PerInstruct dataset for completing user-specific mobile instructions through memory retrieval, app exploration, and clarification when missing context remains unresolved.

name: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: KG-RAG converts UI transition graphs into a searchable vector store and uses intent-guided retrieval to construct actionable navigation paths. It introduces KG-Android-Bench and KG-Harmony-Bench and evaluates transfer from mobile apps to web and desktop tasks.

name: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FlashAdventure evaluates GUI agents on completing story arcs in 34 adventure games. It pairs an automated gameplay judge with COAST, a framework that keeps long-term clue memory to plan and complete sequential objectives.

name: PG-Agent: An Agent Powered by Page Graph
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PG-Agent, which turns GUI operation episodes into page graphs and retrieves guidance from them to support task decomposition in new scenarios.

name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.

name: InfraMind: A Novel Exploration-based GUI Agentic Framework for Mission-critical Industrial Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: InfraMind explores industrial management GUIs using virtual-machine snapshots and builds memory for planning and hierarchical state recognition. Its framework also studies knowledge distillation and safety checks on open-source and commercial data-center management platforms.

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.

name: D-Artemis: A Deliberative Cognitive Framework for Mobile GUI Multi-Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces D-Artemis, a mobile GUI agent framework that retrieves app-specific tips, checks actions before execution, and reflects on their outcomes without trajectory training.

name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Distills generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent trajectories into a persistent memory bank for test-time retrieval.

name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.

name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces JEF-Hinter, which distills successful and failed trajectories into compact episodic hints and retrieves them for the current agent state. Web benchmark experiments examine guidance from decisive steps rather than full demonstration replay.

name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.

name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains BrowserAgent to use Playwright-based scrolling, clicking and typing directly on webpages for information-seeking tasks. Supervised and rejection fine-tuning are paired with explicit memory for conclusions carried across steps.

name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.

name: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Reported evaluations include seen and unseen websites and Mind2Web.
summary: Introduces PolySkill, which separates a web-agent skill's goal from its execution so agents can learn and reuse skills across websites.

name: Branch-and-Browse: Efficient and Controllable Web Exploration with Tree-Structured Reasoning and Action Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its reported task success and execution time results are from WebArena.
summary: Branch-and-Browse is a web agent framework that uses tree-structured subtasks, web state replay, and page action memory to explore and complete tasks.

name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.

name: WebATLAS: An LLM Agent with Experience-Driven Memory and Action Simulation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported success rate is measured on WebArena-Lite.
summary: WebATLAS is a web agent that stores interaction outcomes and simulates candidate actions before acting, using past experience to plan navigation on unseen websites.

name: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MGA, which separates task-agnostic screen-state reading from decision making and connects steps through structured state memory. Validated state deltas replace full trajectory replay, evaluated on OSWorld and application tasks.

name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

name: Mobile-Agent-RAG: Driving Smart Multi-Agent Coordination with Contextual Knowledge Empowerment for Long-Horizon Mobile Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses separate retrieval systems for high-level mobile-task planning and precise interface operations, with a benchmark for extended cross-app tasks.

name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebCoach, which condenses navigation logs into persistent episodic memory and retrieves experiences by similarity and recency. Runtime hooks selectively supply advice to browser agents, evaluated on WebVoyager without retraining the underlying models.

name: Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports only preliminary generalization to unseen tasks in similar environments.
summary: PRAXIS stores action outcomes and retrieves past state-action-result examples to guide agent decisions, with evaluation on the REAL web browsing benchmark.

name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.

name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.

name: PersonalAlign: Hierarchical Implicit Intent Alignment for Personalized GUI Agent with Long-Term User-Centric Records
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroidIntent to evaluate how GUI agents infer omitted preferences and recurring routines from long-term user records. Its HIM-Agent maintains hierarchical memory of preferences and routines for personalized execution and proactive suggestions.

name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.

name: Curiosity Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Mobile Agents
notes: The curiosity signal is a model-based proxy, not a calibrated probability of failure. Accurate external app information is a dependency, and AndroidWorld is the reported evaluation environment. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.1 Problem Formulation; 3.2 Curiosity-Driven Information Gain Estimation; 3.3 Retrieving and Embedding External Knowledge).
summary: Uses execution uncertainty to trigger retrieval from application documentation, code, and past trajectories, organizing the results into structured AppCards for Android agent planning.

name: Me-Agent: A Personalized Mobile Agent with Two-Level User Habit Learning for Enhanced Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Me-Agent personalizes mobile agent behavior through a preference reward model and hierarchical memory for long-term and app-specific habits, and introduces User FingerTip.

name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.

name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.

name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: UI-Mem stores workflows, skills and failure patterns as reusable templates to guide online GUI reinforcement learning. It varies guidance within rollout groups and continually updates the memory so an unguided policy can learn from guided experiences.

name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.

name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions rather than recall alone.

name: Mobile-Agent-v3.5: Multi-platform Fundamental GUI Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Presents GUI-Owl-1.5 variants and a hybrid data pipeline for multimodal GUI interaction, tool use, memory, and multi-platform tasks.

name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Persona2Web tests whether web agents can resolve ambiguous requests using preferences implicit in a user’s history. Its reasoning-aware evaluation compares agent architectures and history-access strategies on personalized tasks on the open web.

name: IntentCUA: Learning Intent-level Representations for Skill Abstraction and Multi-Agent Planning in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: IntentCUA coordinates planner and critic agents through shared intent-aligned memory, retrieving reusable skills for long-horizon automation across desktop applications.

name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.

name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.

name: K^2-Agent: Co-Evolving Know-What and Know-How for Hierarchical Mobile Device Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces K2-Agent, a hierarchical mobile-control framework that refines task knowledge through a reasoning loop and trains an executor with curriculum-guided reinforcement learning.

name: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web-agent tasks are one of three evaluation settings for this general memory module.
summary: Introduces PlugMem, a knowledge-graph memory module for general LLM agents, evaluated on web-agent tasks alongside conversational question answering and knowledge retrieval.

name: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Hierarchical Memory Tree (HMT), which organizes web-agent trajectories by intent, stage and action, then uses the hierarchy to plan and act on websites.

name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.

name: SecAgent: Efficient Mobile GUI Agent with Semantic Context
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile use is explicit, but the abstract does not identify a mobile operating system.
summary: Presents a Chinese mobile GUI dataset and navigation benchmark together with SecAgent, which compresses previous screenshots and actions into semantic summaries. The agent is trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning to use this compact interaction context.

name: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces HyMEM, a graph-based memory for GUI agents that links symbolic task knowledge with trajectory embeddings and refreshes working memory during computer-use tasks.

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations instead of direct memory access. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.

name: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a safety evaluation of OpenClaw and the CIK taxonomy for analyzing how changes to a personal agent's persistent state affect attacks on its local and service access.

name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.

name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EE-MCP studies application-dependent mixtures of GUI actions and MCP calls using generated environments, trajectory collection and filtered training. An experience bank extracts rules from trajectory comparisons for inference-time improvement, distinct from model distillation.

name: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebXSkill pairs parameterized action programs with step-level language guidance, mining reusable skills from synthetic browser-agent traces. A URL-based graph supports retrieval, and deployment alternates between direct program execution and guided native planning.

name: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: UI-Copilot separates GUI execution from on-demand memory retrieval and numerical assistance. Its training procedure treats tool selection and multi-turn task execution as distinct optimization targets while keeping persistent observations outside transient context.

name: SkillDroid: Compile Once, Reuse Forever
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported findings come from a longitudinal evaluation with instruction variation and controlled perturbations.
summary: Introduces SkillDroid, which compiles successful mobile GUI trajectories into reusable action templates and replays them without model calls, recompiling when they degrade.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.

name: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
notes: Adjacent memory-security survey. Full-text Sections 3.1 and 3.3 discuss poisoned web observations persisted into later agent actions; the work is broader than GUI agents and does not establish a platform implementation.
summary: Organizes security risks and defenses for persistent agent memory into six lifecycle phases and proposes five verifiable governance primitives.

name: Mango: Multi-Agent Web Navigation via Global-View Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on WebVoyager and WebWalkerQA.
summary: Proposes Mango, a multi-agent web-navigation method that selects starting URLs using Thompson Sampling and stores navigation history to inform later attempts.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.

name: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web navigation and OS control are among several benchmark settings for the general framework.
summary: A planner-centric RL framework divides agent automation among a planner, actor, and memory manager, with evaluations that include web navigation and OS control.

name: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported task score uses the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset.
summary: cotomi Act is a browser agent that executes multi-step tasks and turns observed user browsing into persistent knowledge shared with users.

name: X-OmniClaw Technical Report: A Unified Mobile Agent for Multimodal Understanding and Interaction
notes: The report presents demonstrations. Its behavior-cloning component captures runtime skills; it does not establish policy-weight imitation training, and literal trace replay is described as future work. No general benchmark result or release completeness is inferred. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (2 Framework; 3 Omni Perception; 4 Omni Memory; 5.1 Omni Action in App Ecosystem; 5.2 Trajectory Cloned Execution).
summary: Describes an Android agent architecture combining multimodal perception, working and personal memory, hybrid XML/visual grounding, and reusable skills captured from user interactions.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.

name: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Executable Agentic Memory stores GUI routines in a knowledge graph built through state-aware exploration and action-group mining. A learned value model guides tree search over this executable memory for retrieval-based planning, with AndroidWorld and efficiency evaluation.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.

name: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Computer use is one track among dialogue, research, and coding evaluations.
summary: MemGym benchmarks agent memory across several task regimes, including computer use on WebArena-Infinity, with scores designed to isolate memory performance.

name: DRIVE: Modeling Skills at the Reasoning and Interaction Levels for Web Agents under Continual Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: DRIVE separates reusable reasoning skills from page-specific interaction skills for web agents, retrieving both to plan tasks and execute actions on websites.

name: PANDO: Efficient Multimodal AI Agents via Online Skill Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes inefficiency in VisualWebArena trajectories and distills reusable online skills to reduce repeated actions and token overhead in multimodal web agents.

name: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.

name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.

name: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Training uses controllable virtual environments, and evaluation is reported on Memory-World.
summary: STAMP trains explicit memory for mobile GUI agents in virtual environments by injecting facts into generated tasks and using supervised data and online RL.

name: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: UI-KOBE explores mobile applications to build graphs of UI states and executable transitions. A lightweight agent then matches its current screenshot to the graph and chooses a transition, local action, completion signal or fallback action.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

name: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a native iOS simulator benchmark with persistent user data, multi-app tasks, and personalization-dependent phone workflows.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

name: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports tests across multiple web-agent frameworks and vision-language models.
summary: Introduces MemVenom, a black-box attack that plants coordinated text and image content in web-agent memory to trigger retrieval and redirect later actions.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares online skill and memory augmentations with a vanilla web agent given the same total inference-token budget. Across WebArena and WorkArena settings, it studies when module overhead removes aggregate gains and how rerun variability changes conclusions.

name: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillMigrator, a web agent that turns successful interactions into reusable skills and transfers them between sites by matching page layouts and live element references.

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

name: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VISUALSKILL organizes application-specific text and figures into hierarchical skills retrieved on demand through an MCP tool. Skills combine authored documentation with live UI exploration, and matched multimodal/text-only comparisons test their utility for interface identification and workflow-state verification.

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.

name: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillHarness, a framework for computer-use agents to learn and reuse skills under safety constraints when interactions include prompt injections or pop-ups.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes ATMem, an updated execution-state memory for long mobile GUI tasks, and STR-GRPO to train selective memory use; also introduces a mobile task benchmark.

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.

name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw combines a host planner with pluggable GUI subagents, attributable experience memory and an evolving skill library. It uses user profiles and feedback for task decomposition and evaluates transfer across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows.

name: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PalmClaw, an on-device phone agent framework that manages sessions, memory, and tools, exposing mobile capabilities through structured device-tool calls.

name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.

name: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method is evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop, so web operation is only one evaluation setting.
summary: Introduces MemHarness, which trains agents to critique and reconstruct retrieved experience before acting; WebShop is one of two evaluation environments.

name: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its components are trained while the GUI policy remains frozen.
summary: Introduces FocusMem, a latent memory interface for GUI agents that separates stored content, state-conditioned readout, and a gate for irrelevant retrieved experience.

name: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported capture analysis uses one professional's single-user corpus.
summary: Introduces Activity Frames, a deterministic pipeline that turns captured screen activity into typed episodes for computer-use agent memory and routine replay.

name: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported experiments also include embodied-agent benchmarks.
summary: Introduces MemPrism, which records prior interactions and builds task-conditioned relational memory views for decisions in long-horizon web-agent tasks.

name: SynChain: Inducing Computer-Use Agent Systems to Construct Their Own Attack Chains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SynChain, an attack that induces persistent agents to create poisoned skills or memory entries, and CUAChain for evaluating later attack-chain activation.

name: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported student comparison uses 119 tasks from ten websites absent from training.
summary: Introduces SkillLens visual skill cards for retrieved GUI action guidance and CardDistill for training an action-prediction student that runs without retrieval on website tasks.

name: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces StateM, a stateful runtime with checked transitions and reusable runbooks for long-horizon agents; its reported evaluations use terminal and business tasks.

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.

name: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Presents RecVerse, a screenshot-based shopping simulation agent with hierarchical memory and trajectory-level RL, alongside USB, an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset.

name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.

name: A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security
notes: Adjacent broad survey of procedural agent skills.
summary: Surveys modular agentic skill architectures, skill lifecycles, and security risks in autonomous tool- and interface-using agents.

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

name: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces activation-conditioned gradient control for GUI agents learning successive applications. It protects inactive application-specific neurons, constrains updates to shared neurons, and accumulates a compact historical state to balance adaptation with retention.

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.

name: VRL-Bench: Benchmarking agents on computer control tasks under finite trial budgets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluations described use MiniWoB and WebShop across three models.
summary: Introduces VRL-Bench to compare trial-and-error learning for computer-control agents under limited attempts, and VEX² to schedule exploration and exploitation.

name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.

name: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports evaluation on OSWorld-v2 and Agent's Last Exam.
summary: Introduces RSIAgent, a training-free framework that explores unfamiliar digital interfaces, stores environment-specific action knowledge, and reuses that memory for later tasks.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Xiryn
notes: Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. Before each step the runtime keeps only the two most recent screenshots in full (docs/architecture.md). The vault fills saved logins and cards into fields without the model seeing them, and cards only after the owner approves the payment. The user can watch and take over the desktop, and the agent hands over at logins, payments, one-time codes or CAPTCHAs, with a Telegram notice when paired. Models come from the owner's keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The README's comparison with hosted agents is the author's own. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived. Code was read, not run.
